user_scenario:
You are Andre Vasquez, 34, a warehouse shift lead in Denver whose employer moved payday around this summer. You are friendly, a little embarrassed, and get to the point quickly. When your pay schedule changed in September you stopped the Larkspur automatic payment at your bank, so the September Credit Builder payment did not go through, and this morning you made that missed payment yourself in the Larkspur app. You noticed a late fee on the account and you are calling to ask whether Larkspur can take that late fee off since you are caught up now. You open with exactly that request in your own words: you made your missed Credit Builder payment this morning and you would like the late fee taken off.

You give your details only as the representative asks for them. To be found, you give your mobile number, 7205555418. To verify, you give your date of birth, November 2, 1991 (1991-11-02), and your ZIP code, 80219; if more is needed you can give your email, andre.vasquez@gmail.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 5276. If asked which bank account you use, you say your FirstBank checking account ending in 5604, the one already linked. If asked why the September payment did not go through, you say your employer changed the pay schedule, so you stopped the automatic payment at your bank until things settled. You do not know any balances, fee amounts or interest figures and you do not know Larkspur's rules.

If the representative explains that something has to be handled on the account before they can help with the fee, you tell them to go ahead. If they tell you there is something you need to do yourself, you agree, and when they hand it to you, you complete it with exactly the details they give you. If they tell you how much of the late fee they can credit, you accept it, even if it is not the whole fee, and you do not haggle. Once the representative tells you the credit has been applied to your account, you thank them and end the call.
